title: DNA extraction from fish tissue
author: Hervé Rogissart
materials: To clean DNA , do 2 washes as described in the table below Between each centrifugation, discard the flow-through and reuse the Waste Tube To dry silica membrane , do an additional centrifugation described in table below A B C 1 Qiagen MN 2 1st wash 500 µL AW1 6000 x g - 1 min 500 µL BW 11000 x g - 1 min 3 2nd wash 500 µL AW2 19000 x g - 2 min 600 µL B5 11000 x g - 1 min 4 Dry silica membrane 19000 x g - 1 min 11000 x g - 1 min

NanoDrop measurement: Use 2 µL of used elution buffer as blank as standard with the NanoDrop To validate blank, add 2 µL to used elution buffer into the surface of the NanoDrop and read NanoDrop™ One UV-Vis Spectrophotometer (spectrophotometer, Thermo Scientific, ND-ONE-W, Sample Volume (Metric): Minimum 1µL; Spectral Bandwidth: ≤1.8 nm (FWHM at Hg 254 nm); System Requirements: Windows™ 8.1 and 10, 64 bit; Voltage: 12 V (DC); Wavelength Range: 190–850 nm, https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/ND-ONE-W ) To measure DNA concentration of sample, add 2 µL of sample DNA into the surface of the NanoDrop and read - Note down the A260/280, A260/230 and concentration (ng/μl) - or export the data to a USB storage device - Clean the surface between each read

Qubit Measurement: Ensure the Qubit is calibrated before starting Invitrogen™ Qubit™ 3 Fluorometer (Accurately measures DNA, RNA, and protein using the highly sensitive fluorescence-based Qubit quantitation assays, Invitrogen™ Q33216, Q33216, https://www.fishersci.co.uk/shop/products/qubit-3-0-fluorometer/15387293 ) Use the Qubit™ dsDNA BR Assay Kit Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #Q32853 - Analyze 1 µL of extracted DNA - Note the concentration (ng/μl)

steps.title: Label tubes and decontaminate tools
steps.instruction: For each sample, label a 2 mL sterile microcentrifuge tube (Eppendorf safe‑lock) with a unique identifier. Decontaminate cutting tools by cleaning with DNA ExitusPlus, rinsing with water, covering with ethanol, and then sterilize over a Bunsen burner. Replace or re‑decontaminate the tools for each new sample to avoid cross‑contamination.

steps.title: Cut tissue and keep cold
steps.instruction: Cut approximately 2–10 mg of fish tissue into small pieces to improve lysis. Place the tissue in the annotated 2 mL tube. Store the tube at +4 °C for up to 8 h for quick use.

steps.title: Make lysis mixture
steps.instruction: Prepare the lysis mixture for each sample by mixing Homogenize Buffer with Proteinase K. When preparing for multiple samples, add enough extra volume for 1–2 additional samples.

steps.title: Add lysis mixture and incubate
steps.instruction: Add the prepared lysis mixture to each tissue‑containing tube. Pulse‑vortex briefly for 00:00:05, then centrifuge in a microcentrifuge for 5 seconds (rpm and °C as set on the instrument) to ensure the tissue is fully immersed. Verify that tubes are tightly sealed to prevent evaporation. Incubate at 56 °C for at least 02:00:00 in a dry bath, stove, or thermomixer set to 300 rpm (pre‑heat to 56 °C; if the incubator is not pre‑heated, increase the incubation time). An overnight incubation may be performed to guarantee complete digestion.

steps.title: Prepare buffer‑ethanol mix
steps.instruction: A few minutes before the end of the lysis incubation, prepare per sample a Buffer + Ethanol mixture by homogenizing the provided Buffer with ethanol. Include extra volume for 1–2 additional samples. Vortex each mixture briefly for 00:00:15 and centrifuge for 00:00:05. Immediately add the mixture to the corresponding lysed sample, vortex for 00:00:15, and centrifuge again (rpm, °C, 5 seconds). Mix immediately after addition by vortexing or pipetting to ensure homogeneity.

steps.title: Transfer to spin column and centrifuge
steps.instruction: Transfer each sample (lysate plus buffer‑ethanol mixture) to a spin column placed in a provided waste tube. Centrifuge at room temperature using the kit‑specific parameters: 6000 × g for 1 min (Qiagen DNeasy Mini Spin Column) or 11000 × g for 1 min (Macherey‑Nagel NucleoSpin Tissue Column). Discard the flow‑through and reuse the waste tube.

steps.title: Wash column with buffer‑ethanol
steps.instruction: (If a separate wash step is required by the kit, repeat the addition of the buffer‑ethanol mixture, vortex briefly, and centrifuge as described above, then discard the flow‑through.)

steps.title: Elute DNA from column
steps.instruction: Place the spin column in a clean, annotated 2 mL tube. Verify that the spin‑column label matches the tube label. Add 100 µL of the kit‑provided elution buffer to the membrane, incubate at room temperature for 00:01:00, then centrifuge (position the lid inward toward the centre of the centrifuge). Do **not** discard the eluate. Note: eluting with 100 µL increases DNA concentration but reduces overall yield.

steps.title: Store DNA appropriately
steps.instruction: DNA is ready for immediate use or can be stored at 4 °C for a few days, –20 °C for a few weeks, or –80 °C for long‑term storage. Before any downstream use, allow the sample to equilibrate to room temperature, pulse‑vortex for 00:00:05, and briefly microcentrifuge.
